intro.label: KARALIS, Spyridon. Alex. Police Ref. 52/117
briefing: On the morning of Friday 11 January 1952, the cotton broker Spyridon Karalis, 61, was found dead in his shuttered office at 14 Rue Stamboul, Alexandria. A charcoal brazier had burned out beside his desk.
The police called it an accident: a man alone, a cold night, closed shutters, charcoal fumes. The file was closed within a week.

In 2024 a box of the family's papers, a watchman's notebook and the original autopsy samples surfaced at the same time. You are the reviewing investigator. Read the desk, question the three people closest to him, and file a charge: who, how, why, and three records that prove it.

victim.name: Spyridon Karalis
victim.summary: Greek Alexandrian cotton broker, 61, widower. Office at 14 Rue Stamboul. Warehouse at Minet el Bassal run by his nephew.

body.subject: Ref 52/117 Karalis: your desk
lines: Good morning,

Three things arrived this winter that make Ref 52/117 worth a second look: the Karalis estate box (deposited by a great-niece), the notebook kept by the building's night watchman (donated by his grandson), and the 1952 autopsy samples, which the university lab has now re-read.
Everything is on your desk. Some records were digitised by the municipal archive: scan the QR stickers to pull the scans up.
The original conclusion was accidental charcoal poisoning. Please tell me if it holds. If it does not, I need a name, a method, a reason, and three records I can put in front of a review board.
The three people closest to Karalis were interviewed in 1952. Their 1952 statements are in the file, and you can put questions to them in the reconstruction room.
Nadia Halim, Archive Review Office
Subject: Death of KARALIS, Spyridon, broker, 61 years, at 14 Rue Stamboul.

The deceased was found at 08.10 on 11 January by his employee Miss L. Sabry, in his office, the street door of which had latched shut. The shutters were closed. A charcoal brazier stood beside the desk and had burned out.
The medical examiner reports death by charcoal fumes, lividity of the cherry type being present.
No sign of violence, no disorder, no money missing from the safe.
Conclusion: accidental death. The deceased lit a brazier against the cold and was overcome. File closed.
Attended 08.40. Office on the first floor, one room with a small washroom. Street door with spring latch, closes and locks itself when pulled.
Deceased seated at the desk, head on his forearms. On the desk: one coffee cup (Turkish, empty, grounds dried), an open ledger, a fountain pen.
Beside the desk: a small clay brazier, ash only. An electric fire in the corner, its plug out of the wall.
Both shutters closed and hooked from inside. Window glass closed.
The deceased's keys in his waistcoat pocket. Safe locked, contents in order per Miss Sabry.
Note: the café below reports the cup was theirs.

body.heading: STATEMENT OF WITNESS (carbon copy). Translated from Arabic.
lines: Name: Laila Sabry, 26, bookkeeper to the deceased for four years. Address: Moharram Bey, with her mother.
I left the office at half past five on Thursday. Mr Karalis was well and was writing letters. He said his nephew might call in the evening.
I went straight home to my mother and stayed in all evening. I did not go out again.
On Friday I arrived at ten past eight, opened the door with my key, and found him. The room smelled of charcoal. I opened the shutters and ran for the watchman.
Mr Karalis never used a brazier. He had trouble with his chest and kept an electric fire.

body.heading: STATEMENT OF WITNESS (carbon copy). Taken in French.
lines: Name: Dr Giulio Ferrante, 58, physician, Rue Nebi Daniel. Friend and doctor of the deceased for twenty years.
I called on Spyridon at about five o'clock on Thursday, a social visit, and left at half past five. He was in good spirits.
Later I was called to the hospital for a delivery and was there most of the night.
Spyridon had a weak chest. I had told him many times to keep away from smoke. I cannot explain the brazier.

body.heading: STATEMENT OF WITNESS (carbon copy). Taken in French.
lines: Name: Aristidis (Aris) Manos, 29, nephew of the deceased, manager of the Karalis warehouse at Minet el Bassal.
I did not see my uncle on Thursday. We had spoken by telephone in the morning about bale weights.
From half past seven until after eleven I was at the Cercle des Négociants, Rue Fouad, playing bridge. Many members saw me.
My uncle was old fashioned and felt the cold. It does not surprise me that he lit a brazier.
My car was in the garage that night. I walked to the club.

body.letterhead: ALEXANDRIA CITY POLICE . NOTE OF INTERVIEW
lines: Name: Hassan Abdel Aal, 15, waiter at the Café Stamboul, ground floor of no. 14.
About ten to eight the khawaga Karalis called down from the stair for coffee. I took it up at a quarter past eight.
The door was half closed. I heard another voice inside, a young man's, speaking Greek. I left the tray on the small table by the door and did not go in.
In the morning I went up for the cups and the police were there.

Session opened at 6 pm, 14 present.

body.note: Political meetings were watched closely in January 1952. Lent by the society's successor association.

body.headline: Women of the gins: a young bookkeeper speaks up
body.subhead: A private meeting in Moharram Bey hears a call for equal wages
columns: On Thursday evening, at a private house in Moharram Bey, some fourteen ladies met to discuss the condition of women employed in the cotton gins of the city.
The most applauded address, delivered at half past eight, came from a young bookkeeper of the Rue Stamboul, Mlle L. S., who spoke without notes for nearly an hour on wages and night shifts.
The meeting closed shortly after ten. We are told the police took an interest in the guest list.
body.also: Also: Broker found dead in his office (page 3).

lines: Alexandria, 9 January 1952. To Mr S. Karalis, Karalis & Co.
Dear Sir, during our annual inspection of the Minet el Bassal warehouse our inspector could not find lots A-17 and A-27, pledged under your receipts Nos. 7741 to 7746 (£E 7,700).
We would be grateful if you would confirm the receipts and the location of the bales by Monday 14 January, failing which we must refer the matter to our legal department.
Translated from French.

envelope.to: Kyrion Dimitrion Lekkas, Odos Solonos 12, Athinai

letter: Βρήκα ότι έξι αποδείξεις αποθήκης με την υπογραφή μου δεν είναι δικές μου.
Το Κ έχει θηλιά, όπως το γράφει ο Άρης, και τα επτά έχουν γραμμή, γαλλικά. Εγώ ποτέ δεν τα γράφω έτσι.
Η τράπεζα ζητά απάντηση ως τη Δευτέρα.
Θα τον δω απόψε στις οκτώ στο γραφείο. Θα του δώσω ως τη Δευτέρα να τα διορθώσει, αλλιώς πηγαίνω ο ίδιος στην τράπεζα.
Αν μου συμβεί κάτι, κράτα αυτό το γράμμα.
translation: My dear Dimitri,
I have found that six warehouse receipts bearing my signature are not mine.
The K has a loop, the way Aris writes it, and the sevens are crossed, French style. I never write them like that.
The bank wants an answer by Monday.
I will see him tonight at eight at the office. I will give him until Monday to put it right, otherwise I go to the bank myself.
If anything happens to me, keep this letter.
Your friend, Spyros
body.note: The addressee died on 6 January 1952. The letter came back unopened and stayed in the estate box for 72 years.

body.heading: Questioned document examination, receipts 7741 to 7746

cells.caption: Looped head stroke, from 'Kom el Dikka'

conclusion: The signatures on receipts 7741 to 7746 were not written by Spyridon Karalis.
The looped K and the crossed 7 match the known hand of Aristidis Manos in every specimen examined.

body.lab: Forensic Toxicology Unit, University Faculty of Medicine
conclusion: A carboxyhaemoglobin level of 11 per cent is not consistent with death by carbon monoxide. It suggests the subject breathed the fumes only briefly, or was already breathing very shallowly.
The barbital level is in the fatal range. Undissolved crystals in coffee point to the drug being taken in a drink, not as tablets.
Cause of death on re-reading: barbital poisoning. The brazier did not kill him.

suspects.name: Aris Manos
sheet: Son of Karalis's late sister Sofia. Runs the Karalis warehouse at Minet el Bassal.
Member of the Cercle des Négociants. Drives a grey car. Known at the bridge tables.
Sole heir after the deceased's death, per the 1949 will.
suspects.openingLine: (adjusts his cufflinks) Seventy years later and still you want to talk about my uncle. Naturally. Ask.

questions.text: Where were you on the evening of 10 January?
When did you last see your uncle?
The club register says you signed out at 19.55. Where did you go?
Your car was photographed outside no. 14 at 8.20. Explain that.
Why did you buy a brazier and charcoal at nine that night?
Who collected the Veronal from the Pharmacie Centrale on 8 January?
The 2024 lab found Veronal, not smoke, killed him. What was in his coffee?

suspects.name: Dr Giulio Ferrante
sheet: Italian Alexandrian physician, friend of the deceased for twenty years.
Owed the deceased £E 400 on a note falling due 15 January 1952.
Prescribed Veronal for the deceased in December 1951.
suspects.openingLine: (sighs, folds his hands) Ah. Spyridon. Madonna, what a waste. Ask what you like, caro, I am an old man with nothing left to hide. Almost nothing.

questions.text: What time did you visit Karalis on 10 January?
The watchman saw you arrive at 6.10 and leave angry at 6.40. Why lie about the time?
Tell me about the 400 pounds you owed him.
You prescribed him Veronal. Who else knew about it?
Where were you after seven that evening?

suspects.name: Laila Sabry
sheet: Bookkeeper to the deceased for four years. Held a key to the office.
Found the body at 08.10 on 11 January.
Educated at the Lycée, reads French and English, keeps the office books.
suspects.openingLine: (straightens the papers in front of her) Good afternoon. I told the police everything in 1952. I will tell you the same, if you are polite.

questions.text: Where did you go after leaving the office at 5.30?
Who was expected at the office that evening?
The society minutes say you spoke at 8.30 in Moharram Bey. Why say you were home?
What was the 12 pound advance for?
Did Karalis ever mention trouble with the bank?

hints.text: Did Karalis even use a brazier? Check what his doctor and his bookkeeper say about his chest.
The 2024 toxicology re-reading gives a carbon monoxide figure. Compare it with the fatal level.
11 per cent carbon monoxide cannot kill. Veronal in his coffee did. The brazier was staged afterwards.

hints.question: Who was in the office that evening?

hints.text: The café order book records how many coffees went up.
The night watchman kept a notebook that the police never collected. Read the translation.
The doctor came at 6.10 and left at 6.40. A man in a grey overcoat came at 8.05 and came back at 9.20 with a basket.
Members of the Cercle signed out as well as in.
Use the magnifier on the wedding photograph, then scan the traffic registry sticker.
Aris left the club at 19.55 and came back at 21.55. His grey Hillman, plate 4417, was outside no. 14 at 8.20.

hints.question: Why would anyone want Karalis dead?

hints.text: Read the letter from the bank, then break the seal on the returned letter.
Compare the K and the 7 on the warehouse receipt with known handwriting.
Aris forged six receipts worth £E 7,700. His uncle found out and gave him until Monday.
Both the doctor and the bookkeeper lied about their evening. Lies are not proof of murder.
Find where each of them was between 8 and 10 pm. One record is from a hospital, one from a meeting.
Ferrante was delivering a baby from 19.15 to 23.40. Laila spoke at a women's meeting at 20.30 and stayed until 22.15.
